fig4v2.text: Fig. 4. E7, 16 confirmation weeks (trace lender, overflow accounting); all-fallback: 35,010 USD/week (median). Medians, 95% intervals. (a) Segments: component medians, scaled; provision for peak: 24.3. (b) Per week, least of H1's set minus Sublet: trace cost (H1: median 0.052 [0.038, 0.080]), W0 (>0 in 16/16, H2); RetroRenting, τ≥1 h minus Sublet: W0 (<0 in 3/16; H2b fails). (c) Grey: all-fallback; critical-ratio renting alone coincides with Sublet. Weeks: rotations of one series; statistics descriptive; RetroRenting-style, lagged (H1's set): supplement.

sf_e3_v2.text: The sharing study on its confirmation instances, reported as measured (H5 failed at b = 1): cost over the shared lower bound against the borrowers per LLM b (u = 8, mu/beta~ = 1, one day), (a) shared and (b) siloed replicas (dashed). Each point is the median over 4 config seeds (301, 302, 303, 304) with the range over the seeds (the registered bootstrap's 95% interval, equal to the range in every cell); intervals narrower than a marker are hidden by it, and every one is in Table e3_v2. Lagged RetroRenting + one-way guard: the lagged RetroRenting-style rule in the one-way guard at B0 = 10% of all-fallback. Stars: siloed OPT / shared OPT (the median of the seeds' bracket points, with the bracket ends over the seeds); grey: b, the copy bound on siloed OPT (each borrower can copy the whole shared plan), attained on C3-P7's instance (PROVEN, elementary).

sf_e7_intensity.text: Stress-intensity curves of the 12 policies of part second on weeks 301--304 (4 weeks, policy seed 0): cost over all-fallback against the reclaim probability $p$ of the i.i.d. lender per site and slot, on the grid $p\in\{0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.34, 0.5, 0.8, 1\}$ ($p=0$ is the honoring lender L-hon; part main's runs and part second's merged). Medians over the 4 weeks with their ranges; the weeks are rotations of one series. Sublet is drawn and labeled in every panel; the grey line marks all-fallback. The $p$ axis has a square-root scale (minor ticks: the grid's other points), and the series of a panel are offset horizontally by 1.4 pt each, so that equal medians stay apart. Critical-ratio renting's medians lie within 0.0001 of Sublet's at every $p$. At $p=0$, Greedy + guard; Greedy renting; and Greedy, back-off share the median 0.632. At $p\ge0.5$, Lagged RetroRenting + one-way guard ($B_0=10\%$ of the all-fallback bill) and RetroRenting-style differ by at most 0.03. Each policy's first $p$ with a cost above 1, on every week, is in Table~\ref{tab:e7v2-crossings}.

sf_e7_decomp.text: The ablations of critical-ratio renting (A9, Sublet's inner policy) and the transplants against Sublet on weeks 301--316 of part main (16 weeks, policy seed 0): per week the difference from Sublet of the cost over all-fallback under the trace lender ($\Delta r_0$) and of the worst cost over the five stress lenders ($\Delta W_0$); medians over the weeks with 95\% week-bootstrap intervals (10,000 resamples, seed 20261031; descriptive, the weeks being rotations of one series). Sublet is the origin; positive is worse. (a) Critical-ratio renting and its ablations, with $\Delta W_0$ on a scale linear within $\pm0.02$ and logarithmic beyond; (b) greedy renting with critical-ratio renting's notice layer and with Sublet's guard, RetroRenting-style with critical-ratio renting's contract rule and make-before-break (arrows from the base policy, in its color), and Sublet's guard without projection. Critical-ratio renting and its ablation ``no insurance'' have Sublet's medians and intervals (one name). The ablations ``no commitment rule'' and ``no site marking'' have a lower $W_0$ than Sublet: median $\Delta W_0$ $-$0.012 and $-$0.018, respectively (intervals below 0), at a median $\Delta r_0$ of 0.0009 and 0.0014. Sublet, one-way: in weeks 301, 306, 309, 311, 313 and 316, in which its guard aborts in every run (42 of its 112 runs of part main), $\Delta r_0$ is 0.44--0.51 and $\Delta W_0$ 0.21--0.29, right of the drawn range (its name gives the count); in the other 10 weeks it equals Sublet. Sublet, one-way's interval on $\Delta r_0$ reaches 0.45 (arrow). Per-week values in Table~\ref{tab:e7v2-weeks}.

sf_e7_boundary.text: Boundary conditions of part second on weeks 301--304 (4 weeks, policy seed 0), one row per policy: the median cost over all-fallback with its range over the weeks (the weeks being rotations of one series) under (a) L-vr, the trace lender with buffer violations turned into reclaims without notice: no buffer violation occurred in its 48 runs, so its cost equals the trace lender's for every policy on every week; (b) L-rf, the trace lender refusing purchases on unavailable layers; (c) L-ad, the adaptive lender, which announces every lease at the end of its guaranteed period (on these weeks its cost equals that of the eager lender L-eg and of the i.i.d. lender at $p=1$ for every policy: each announces every revocable lease when its guaranteed period ends); (d) the trace lender with the P99.9 lease buffer; (e) the trace lender with demand lagged by one slot, for the policy of its row on slot $t-1$'s demand (RetroRenting-style: its lagged build), each marker in the lagged variant's style. Grey ticks: the row's policy under the trace lender on the same weeks (part main); grey line: all-fallback. Panel (c) has its own $x$ range. Per-week values in Tables~\ref{tab:e7v2-boundary} and \ref{tab:e7v2-lag}; the E5 menus and the gap days in Tables~\ref{tab:e7v2-e5} and \ref{tab:e7v2-gap}.

sf_e7_grid_dev.text: Part grid, development-exposed (continuity, not a confirmation result). (a) The end-to-end week at 4 alignments under the trace lender: cost over all-fallback, the median over the policy seeds with their range; Critical-ratio renting ran policy seed 0 only. Ranges narrower than a marker are hidden by it (the largest is 0.017); every entry is in Table e7v2_grid. (b), (c) The guard study's held-out cells of 4 instances: the median cost under the trace lender and W0, the largest median over the stress lenders; Greedy + one-way guard, Lagged RetroRenting + one-way guard and the lagged RetroRenting-style rule from the guard study's summary (its cells). In every panel the series sit left to right in the legend's order, read down its columns. Criterion S: W0 <= 1.05 on every instance. It holds for Sublet; Greedy + guard; Greedy + one-way guard; Lagged RetroRenting + one-way guard. It fails for Critical-ratio renting; RetroRenting-style, lagged. Criterion T is not computable: part grid runs no renting baseline (BL1, BL2, BL5) on these cells (the guard study's own T for its rows is in Table e7v2_q44).

sf_fam_v2.text: The guard study's family instances and the confirmation's fresh instances (policy seeds 13-22): ALG/OPT against the exact OPT, each instance's mean over its seeds, the median over the instances with their range; (a) F1 and F2 by lender, (b) F3 against beta under the eager lender; the series sit left to right in the legend's order, read down its columns. Critical-ratio renting equals RR-renew on 328 of the 328 counted pairs (H4), and Sublet projects in 0 of them; RR-renew and Marking are in the tables. Equal at every instance: (a) Sublet = Critical-ratio renting = Critical-ratio renting, no insurance; Greedy + guard = Greedy + one-way guard; (b) Greedy + guard = Greedy + one-way guard. On F3 Sublet aborts in 39 of its 100 runs; Greedy + guard in 68 of 100; Greedy + one-way guard in 68 of 100; Lagged RetroRenting + one-way guard in 100 of 100 (Table fam_v2_f3).

sf_e7_links.text: MS4's E7 result on the development-exposed alignments 1, 2, 3, 4 (policy seeds 0, 1, 2; not a confirmation result): saving over all-fallback (overflow accounting) against the cross-region links of the routing graph, medians with MS4's 95% bootstrap intervals. Lagged RetroRenting + one-way guard (filled markers) is the lagged RetroRenting-style rule (open markers) in the one-way guard at B0 = 10% of all-fallback. Their medians are equal at every number of cross-region links.

table3_v2.text: End-to-end cost per policy, medians of 16 confirmation weeks (301--316; trace lender, full menu, $\mu/\tilde\beta=1$). ALG/LB: the first day of weeks 301--304 (5-min routing, reduced menu) over the LP bound, an upper bound on the ratio to the offline optimum. $p^\ast$: lower median over weeks 301--304 of the first i.i.d.\ reclaim probability with $r_0>1$ (0.00: $r_0>1$ already without reclaims; none: $r_0\le1$ at every $p\le1$; $>$0.2: likewise, but only $p\le0.2$ ran). Guarded rows: per-group allowance $\min\{\Wk,\mathrm{LB}'\}$. Theorem~\ref{thm:fullmodel}'s bound held in 448 of 448 guarded runs (trace, five stress and honoring lenders; 112 of Lagged RetroRenting + one-way guard (\mbox{$B_0=10\%$} of the all-fallback bill); cases (a) 382, (b) 66); Corollary~\ref{cor:ratio}(b) holds for Sublet and Sublet, one-way, on core instances (Lemma~\ref{lem:projection}(e)); Sublet, one-way aborted in 42 of 112 runs (under the trace lender in 6 of 16 weeks, at the all-fallback bill; in the rest at Sublet's cost); Sublet and Greedy + guard in none. Primary baselines (H1): Greedy renting; Greedy, back-off; RetroRenting-style; Per-borrower ski rental; SpotHedge-style, \mbox{$N_{\mathrm{Extra}}=0$}; CoCaR-style; and RetroRenting-style, lagged (supplement). Provision for peak: 24.3 times the all-fallback bill in overflow accounting.
